blocks.text: The hidden cost of bad requirements

When you fail to track requirements, you lose the link between the business goal and the code. This creates a massive financial burden. Studies indicate that 60% of rework costs stem from incomplete or incorrect requirements. You end up building things that do not solve the actual problem. This is not just a documentation issue. It is a fundamental risk to your organization.

If you are a computer systems analyst working on a Mac, you likely use tools like Jira or Notion. The problem is that these tools often become graveyards for information. Without a clear traceability matrix, you cannot see the impact of a change. A small change in a feature request can break three other dependencies. You only find this out during testing, when it is too expensive to fix.

items: Ambiguity: Vague terms like user-friendly allow for conflicting interpretations.
Constant Change: Without traceability, changes lead to architectural drift.
Communication Gaps: Stakeholders often describe solutions instead of the core problem.
Time Pressure: Teams skip the discovery phase to start coding faster.

blocks.text: The root cause is rarely the software you use. It is a thinking gap. You might be focused on the tool rather than the alignment. When you skip the discovery phase, you are building on sand. If you are in a regulated industry, you must follow your company policy on data handling. Never put sensitive client or patient data into public AI tools.
Fixes that work for any analyst

You do not need to buy expensive software to start improving requirement traceability. Start by creating a simple Requirements Traceability Matrix in Excel or a shared document. List every business requirement and map it to a specific technical task. If a task does not link to a requirement, ask why you are doing it.
Review your requirements every week. Check if the business objective has shifted. If it has, update your matrix immediately to prevent the team from working on obsolete features.
blocks.title: Weekly review

blocks.text: Another fix is to hold a validation meeting. Present your requirements to the developers and the stakeholders at the same time. Ask the developers to explain how they see the requirement. You will quickly find the ambiguities in the language. Use this feedback to rewrite the requirements until everyone agrees on the outcome.
How Lazur helps you track requirements

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It helps you stay in the flow by answering questions about your current screen. When you are looking at a complex Jira ticket or a long Notion document, hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur to explain a specific section. It can help you identify missing dependencies by comparing your notes against the active window.
A daily routine for better traceability

items: Morning: Review the traceability matrix for open items.
Midday: Validate new requirements with stakeholders.
Afternoon: Audit technical tasks against the business objectives.
End of day: Log changes and update the documentation.
